description: Sends one text to a chat: a person, a group or Note to Self (the user's own account id as the chat). `chat` is a chat id from signal_chat_read or signal_contact_read check, never a name or a number. `text` is sent exactly as given, surrounding blank space trimmed, at most 4000 characters. `reply_to` quotes a message of that chat by its id; one that was deleted or has disappeared cannot be quoted. A group the user left is refused. The chat's disappearing timer applies by itself. The result means Signal accepted it, not that it was delivered or read; for a group it says how many members it reached and lists those it did not. A failure `uncertain` means the message may have gone out: check the chat on the phone, never send it again blindly. A send is recorded in the local mirror; `errors.record` says when that failed although the message was sent.

account.description: The account label; absent picks the only linked label.

chat.description: The chat id, from signal_chat_read or signal_contact_read check: a person's account id, or `group:<id>`. The user's own account id is Note to Self.

reply_to.description: The id of a message of that chat to quote, `<account id>:<sent time in ms>` as a read gives it.

text.description: The text exactly as it should arrive; surrounding blank space is trimmed, and what is left is 1 to 4000 characters.

name: signal_message_send

errors.description: Set when the message was sent but could not be written to the mirror.

id.description: The sent message's id, `<account id>:<sent time in ms>`.

not_reached.description: The recipients it did not reach, by account id, with the reason in plain words.

id.description: The member's account id; absent when Signal did not name one.

reached.description: A group (or a send with a failure entry): how many recipients Signal accepted it for.

time.description: When it was sent, in local time with offset.

title: Send a message
